data.name: Charity
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ‘charis’, meaning ‘grace’ or ‘kindness’. Charity is the virtue of giving and loving unselfishly. In Christianity, it is considered one of the theological virtues.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of selflessness and compassion, reminding us to give love and kindness to others.
data.numerology_meaning: Peaceful, sensitive, and empathetic individuals who value harmony and balance.

in_hebrew.name: חסד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: חסד (Chesed) היא מידת אהבה, רחמים, וסליחה, המצויה באלוהים. בקבלה, חסד נחשבת העליונה מבין הספירות. במקרא, חסד היא תכונה של אלוהים, המופיעה בבראשית א, 6, שם האלוהים מתאר את שאר רברבי, שהיא אחת מן השפות הקדומות, ומשמעותה - רחמים, חסד, אהבה.

in_greek.name: Ἀγάπη
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἀγάπη (Agapē) ἐστὶν ἡ ἡνωμένη μετὰ τὸν Θεόν, ἡ ἀγάπη, ἡ ἔλεος, ἡ ἀπαρχή. Ἀγάπη ἐστὶν οὐ τὸν ἄνθρωπον σῶσαι, ἀλλά τὸν Θεόν σώζειν. Ἀγάπη ἐστὶν ἡ ἔλεος τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἀγάπη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_latin.name: Caritas
in_latin.long_meaning: Caritas est amor, misericordia, et indulgentia Dei. Caritas est radix omnis boni. Caritas est voluntas Dei, qui est in Christo Jesu. Caritas non facit injuriam, sed omnia facit propter Deum.

in_english.name: Charity
in_english.long_meaning: Charity is derived from the Greek word agapē, meaning love, kindness, and generosity. In Christianity, charity is one of the seven virtues and is considered a manifestation of God's love. It is the selfless concern for the well-being of others and is often associated with acts of kindness, generosity, and mercy. Charity is also a key aspect of Christian tradition and is often seen as a way to demonstrate one's love for God and others.

biblical_reference.note: Charity is one of the three virtues, along with faith and hope, that are considered essential for the Christian life.

data.cultural_impact: Charity as a name is synonymous with generosity, compassion, and selflessness. This name carries a powerful connotation for its possessor, signifying a deep commitment to helping others, and a kind-hearted spirit. Historically, numerous charitable organizations, hospitals, and foundations have taken the name in honor of its meanings and the positive associations it holds in society.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian theology, Charity is considered to be the virtue of loving God above all else and loving one's neighbor as oneself. Through this act of selfless giving, individuals are able to emulate the love, kindness, and compassion of God. Ultimately, Charity represents the divine force that binds communities together and fosters a sense of love, connection, and belonging.

historical_references.reference: Saint Charity of the Hospitals, also known as Charity of Monza, was an Italian nun who lived in the 14th century.
Charity, in Christianity, is the virtue of loving others as oneself and is concerned with the welfare of others.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Charity remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Charity, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Charity meaning "Love, kindness, generosity" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Charity is the virtue that motivates us to give selflessly, to love unconditionally, and to serve generously. It is the bond that unites us to God and to one another, and the foundation of a just and compassionate society.
